edges.description: Marden-Walker syndrome is proposed as an etiologic possibility in the fetal akinesia/hypokinesia deformation sequence (FADS), presenting at birth with multiple congenital joint contractures.

Fixed flexion contracture of the fingers (camptodactyly) is reported among the congenital contracture manifestations of Marden-Walker syndrome; specific intermediate biomechanics are not detailed in the cited clinical report.
Kyphoscoliosis is a defining axial skeletal feature reported alongside joint contractures in Marden-Walker syndrome; the intermediate pathomechanics are not specified in the cited source.
Decreased muscular bulk is reported alongside congenital joint contractures and immobile facies in classic Marden-Walker syndrome.

Absent deep tendon reflexes (areflexia) are reported alongside congenital joint contractures and decreased muscular bulk in clinical Marden-Walker syndrome; the underlying neuromuscular mechanism is not established in the cited report.
An immobile, mask-like face is a hallmark clinical feature of Marden-Walker syndrome reported in cases classified within the fetal akinesia/hypokinesia deformation sequence.
Blepharophimosis accompanies the mask-like face in the classic clinical description of Marden-Walker syndrome; the specific periocular developmental mechanism is not detailed in the cited source.
Micrognathia is a defining craniofacial feature of Marden-Walker syndrome reported in cases placed within the fetal akinesia/hypokinesia deformation sequence.
Cleft palate is a characteristic craniofacial malformation of Marden-Walker syndrome; the intermediate palatal developmental mechanism is not detailed in the cited source.
A high-arched palate is a characteristic craniofacial feature of Marden-Walker syndrome; the intermediate palatal developmental mechanism is not detailed in the cited source.
Abnormal posterior fossa and hindbrain morphogenesis manifests as Dandy-Walker malformation (often with hydrocephalus).

nodes.description: PIEZO2 is the principal mechanotransduction channel of proprioceptive sensory neurons innervating muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs. In gain-of-function Piezo2 E2799del knock-in mice (modeling the human DA5 E2727del variant), conditional expression in Pvalb-Cre proprioceptive neurons is sufficient to induce hindlimb contractures and shortened tendons, whereas conditional expression in Prrx1-Cre limb mesenchyme (osteoblasts, chondrocytes, tenocytes, and fibroblasts) produces normal joints and tendon lengths. The defect depends on peripheral sensory-neuron activity during a postnatal developmental critical window (between P7 and P21 in mice): local intramuscular botulinum toxin (Botox) injection at P7-P10 rescues the joint and tendon defects, whereas motor-endplate blockade with alpha-bungarotoxin does not, and ex vivo stretch-evoked muscle spindle afferent firing at P7 is not significantly changed. The authors conclude that overactive PIEZO2 acts via ectopic efferent activity (increased exocytosis) from afferent mechanosensory nerve endings rather than increased reflex motor drive. This node is PROVISIONAL for Marden-Walker syndrome because the mouse models a DA5 allele during a postnatal window, whereas human MWS contractures are congenital and MWS is genetically heterogeneous.
nodes.id: Excessive Mechanotransduction in Proprioceptive Sensory Neurons

nodes.description: Clinical and nosological framing for Marden-Walker syndrome as one etiologic possibility within the genetically heterogeneous fetal akinesia/hypokinesia deformation sequence (FADS), based on clinical reports of pregnancies complicated by feeble fetal movements and polyhydramnios followed at birth by multiple joint contractures, decreased muscular bulk, immobile mask-like facies, micrognathia, and palatal anomalies. Because MWS is genetically heterogeneous (with PIEZO2 mutations identified in only a subset of MWS families) and the Piezo2 gain-of-function mouse model develops contractures postnatally via sensory-neuron efferent activity and tendon shortening rather than in utero akinesia or primary muscle pathology, this clinical FADS node is modeled separately rather than as a direct downstream consequence of the PIEZO2 sensory-neuron mechanism.

nodes.description: Mouse carrying the mouse equivalent of the human distal arthrogryposis type 5 variant E2727del, expressed constitutively or restricted by Cre driver to proprioceptive neurons (Pvalb), all sensory neurons (Advillin, inducible), or limb mesenchyme (Prrx1). Constitutive and proprioceptor-restricted mice develop hindlimb contractures and shortened tendons during a postnatal developmental window (between P7 and P21) without skeletal muscle histological abnormalities or altered muscle fiber diameters, whereas mesenchyme-restricted mice do not. Intramuscular botulinum toxin injected into the hindlimb at postnatal days 7 to 10, or a maternal/postnatal diet enriched in eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), which accelerates PIEZO2 inactivation, reduced the tendon and joint defects.

nodes.description: PIEZO2 is a mechanically activated, non-selective cation channel that transduces mechanical force into ionic current in proprioceptive and somatosensory neurons. The disease-associated heterozygous variants in the dominant PIEZO2 spectrum are gain-of-function: in cellular electrophysiology of distal arthrogryposis type 5 alleles (E2727del and I802F), PIEZO2-dependent mechanically activated currents recover faster from inactivation (with E2727del also slowing inactivation), producing increased channel activity in response to a given mechanical stimulus. The effect is not constitutive channel opening or cytotoxicity but an altered mechanotransduction gain. The node name is shared with the Gordon syndrome entry because the molecular lesion is the same.

nodes.description: In gain-of-function Piezo2 knock-in mice, average hindlimb tendon length is significantly reduced compared to wild-type littermates, and the authors propose that shortened tendons drive the joint contractures. Proprioceptive nerve-ending morphology in muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs is intact and skeletal muscle fiber diameters are unchanged, indicating that overactive PIEZO2 impairs tendon and joint development rather than causing primary histological muscle abnormalities. In the mouse model, inducible sensory-neuron expression defines a critical postnatal developmental period between days 7 and 21 during which excessive mechanotransduction causes limb malformation, whereas human MWS contractures are congenital.
